1606.note: BNE Digital MSS/20210/46 (Diego Crolope, 12 Jan 1681) was viewed in Chrome on 5 Nov 2026: two leaves written almost wholly in a letter-substitution cipher with a few numerals, a clear-text Spanish closing paragraph with the signature, and no decipherment on or with it.

seen.where: BNE Digital card https://bnedigital.bne.es/bd/es/card?id=8b0f5fc5-5240-4104-8392-76cf341135c4 (signature MSS/20210/46, 2 h., 1681, bdh0000173166) and viewer https://bnedigital.bne.es/bd/es/viewer?id=8b0f5fc5-5240-4104-8392-76cf341135c4, viewer pages 2, 3 and 4 viewed in my own Chrome tab on 5 Nov 2026 (the viewer opened normally; the 3 Nov block did not recur).
seen.extent: 5 viewer images: 1 cover, 2 a full page of about 38 lines of cipher, 3 a two-page opening of about 35 lines per page (cipher, ending in a clear-text Spanish paragraph and the signature 'Diego Crolope'), 4 the verso with bleed-through, 5 back cover; roughly 120-150 cipher lines.
seen.cipher: Image 2 (viewed): word-spaced cipher in Latin letters (frequent one-letter word 'z', short words 'fa', 'ag', 'xe'), a few numerals such as 18, 26 and 399, no Spanish plaintext between the lines; image 3: the same cipher, then about ten lines of clear Spanish ('...remite a Vm. ...') dated 12 Jan 1681 and signed 'Diego Crolope'. BNE's card has no cipher note (only 'Nombre de remitente dudoso || Manchas de humedad'); the interlinear space and margins hold no decipherment and no key is filed with the 2 h.

seen.cipher: Card text (quoted): '10270-81 C,MIS.WCD. Nov.9-17 Enc.2 messages which have been deciphered. Code used in these messages was a disc[...] The Tismera message is being deciphered by use of an old system of Ger.shorthand. Translation & deciphering goes very slow.' The decipherments of the two messages were enclosed with the file; the Tismera message is shorthand rather than a cipher and has no recorded result.
